# The ECI frontier has advanced by 14 points per year since the introduction of reasoning models

Cite

By Alexander Barry

Following the introduction of the first reasoning models (OpenAI’s o1-mini and o1-preview) in September 2024, the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) frontier has advanced linearly by 14 points per year, compared with 6 points per year for non-reasoning models.

## Learn more about this graph

See our report “Have AI Capabilities Accelerated?” for details on the methodology we used to detect that the ECI (and some other measures of AI capability) had a trend break with reasoning models.

### Data

For this analysis we used the ECI data as accessed on 1 September 2026. The exact data used can be downloaded below.

Note for this analysis we did not extend the ECI to consider models that released before January 1st 2023, unlike our two prior works (1, 2), as we wanted to directly use the current ECI results.

### Methodology

The central trends are simple linear fits over each model that was SOTA on release for reasoning/non-reasoning models.

For simplicity we categorise every model released up to and including GPT-4.5 (27 February 2025) as non-reasoning, except a specific list:

  * o1-preview
  * o1-mini
  * o1
  * DeepSeek-R1
  * Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking (Jan 2025)
  * o3-mini
  * Claude 3.7 Sonnet

After GPT-4.5 we treat every model as reasoning.

The 90% interval on each rate comes from the same 500 refits, spanning the 5th to 95th percentiles of their slopes.

## Preprocessing

To be used in our methodology, benchmarks need to be scored on a 0-1 scale (or equivalently, 0% to 100%). For benchmarks where random guessing would score above 0 (e.g. those with multiple choice responses), we rescale so that random guessing performance is scaled to zero. For benchmarks with a known error rate, we also rescale scores so that the maximum possible score is scaled to one. For example, FrontierMath v1 was found to have an error rate of 43% across Tiers 1-3, and 40% for Tier 4, so its scores are rescaled accordingly. Where a model has been evaluated on both v1 and v2 of a FrontierMath benchmark, only the v2 score enters the fit.

In order to capture the upper end of each model’s capabilities, we aggregate across model evaluation settings (e.g. thinking effort and inference provider), taking the highest score for each benchmark. We only aggregate over models released on the same day with the same name (e.g. we do not aggregate across versions of GPT-4o released on different days). We drop any models with fewer than 4 benchmark scores from our model fit, to avoid low-certainty estimates. We also exclude models released before 2023 due to data sparsity; we hope to increase coverage in the future.

# Overview

The Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) combines scores from many different AI benchmarks into a single “general capability” scale, allowing comparisons between models even over timespans long enough for single benchmarks to reach saturation.

ECI is a composite metric which uses scores from over 50 distinct benchmarks to generate a single, general capability scale. At a high level, ECI stitches together its component benchmarks, determining their relative difficulty by making comparisons wherever models are evaluated on multiple benchmarks. Individual models obtain higher ECI scores if they perform better on harder benchmarks.
